Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements - Finly

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and next steps so we're aligned.

Key pain points you called out:
- p95 latency spikes on inference during market open (~15:30 ET) that degrade the streaming UX for traders.
- Backend concurrency limits: current in-house stack struggles above ~180 concurrent streaming sessions; you see queuing and tokenization backpressure.
- Cost unpredictability when load spikes; want clear cost per 1k streaming tokens under high-concurrency scenarios.

Current stack:
- Model: finly/bart-trading-v2 (custom variant) hosted on self-managed GPU pool (A100x) behind a Node.js streaming service.
- Frontend: WebSocket-based streaming consumer used by trader dashboards.
- Orchestration: Kubernetes with HPA, but cold-starts and KV cache misses are common.

Success criteria (as discussed):
1) p95 generation latency <= 250ms for single-shot queries and <= 350ms for streaming token delivery during peak.
2) Seamless streaming UX under 500 concurrent active streams during peak (initial goal: 300).
3) Predictable cost model: target < $X per 1k streaming tokens (we'll refine after perf run).

Proposed next steps we agreed on:
- Redwood runs a short controlled perf test on a mirrored dataset (non-PII) to measure p95 across model variants and batching policies. (Action: Redwood / Aditya)
- Share the latency matrix and a short perf playbook for streaming (Action: Redwood / Marissa).
- Finly to provide a sample request distribution and a short list of top 10 prompts (Action: Alex).
- Follow-up technical call to review perf run and proposed deployment configs (Schedule: next week).

Attachments: I've attached a short discovery notes PDF and a latency matrix worksheet (skeleton) to collect your numbers.

If I mis-captured anything, please correct. Otherwise I'll loop Aditya in to set up the perf run and propose time slots for the follow-up.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Discovery recap: p95 latency, streaming UX & concurrency requirements - Finly

Alex / Marissa — quick technical note ahead of the perf run. A couple of things we'll validate and recommend:

1) Kernel/quantization choices: for your custom bart variant we'll try int8 and a mixed-precision run to see p95 impact; often int8 reduces cost but can add small variance in tail latency.
2) Batching policy: we'll test continuous batching with adaptive timeouts (5-15ms windows) vs fixed micro-batch sizes to measure p95 under bursty arrival.
3) KV cache warming: we recommend a short warm-up phase to populate KV cache for the top request patterns you'll share — this often trims 50-100ms off p95 in streaming flows.
4) Session routing: propose reserving a pool for high-priority streams during market open to keep perceived latency consistent.

For the perf run we'll need:
- A 10-15 minute synthetic replay of your market-open arrival curve (we can replay via k6/Locust).
- Example prompts and token distributions (Alex will upload).
- Indication if there are any SLAs that require isolated capacity (e.g., legal/regulatory).

I'll set up two small runs: one on a standard Redwood shared-hosted setup and one on a dedicated pool config (similar GPU count you're running) so we can compare cost/latency trade-offs. Will share scripts + expected metrics ahead of the run.

Thanks — I'll propose perf run times in the calendar invite.

Aditya Rao
